source_meta._title: You can retain entities' shaders by running the "/kill" command while in spectator mode

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 14w05a in a disposable singleplayer world using the integrated server. Use a non-Hardcore Creative world with commands enabled for setup, then enter Spectator mode for the trigger. A Superflat world and Normal difficulty are practical choices that keep the Creeper easy to locate and prevent it from disappearing because of Peaceful difficulty. Do not use external shader mods or shader packs.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected snapshot Minecraft 14w05a; do not substitute the listed fix snapshot Minecraft 14w05b.
Use a new or otherwise disposable non-Hardcore singleplayer world so that the player can respawn after executing /kill.
Commands must be enabled. When creating the world, select Creative mode and ensure Allow Cheats is ON.
Set difficulty to Easy, Normal, or Hard rather than Peaceful so the summoned Creeper remains present.
Use first-person perspective before beginning the command sequence.
Know the current bindings for Open Chat, Attack/Destroy, and movement. Their defaults are T, left-click, and W/A/S/D.

After entering the Creeper's viewpoint, do not press the dismount control, F4, or any perspective/game-mode shortcut before executing /kill. Those actions may detach the camera or toggle the entity shader.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the exact historical snapshot Minecraft 14w05a, launch it, and wait for its main menu to appear.
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the main menu running snapshot 14w05a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new disposable world. Select Creative as the game mode, ensure Hardcore is not selected, open More World Options, turn Allow Cheats ON, and optionally select Superflat to make the Creeper easy to locate. Create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The world-loading screen begins and the selected world is non-Hardcore with commands available.

steps.action: Wait until the world has fully loaded. If the difficulty is Peaceful, press Esc, open Options, click the Difficulty button until it displays Normal, select Done, and return to the game. Do not continue until surrounding terrain is rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Difficulty: Normal -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in a loaded area, and the difficulty is Normal rather than Peaceful.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the historical 14w05a summon command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The command places a Creeper three blocks away along the positive Z axis.
steps.success_cue: A Creeper has been created close to the player; turn around if necessary until it is visible.

steps.action: While still in Creative mode, move or turn as needed so that the Creeper is clearly visible and close enough to target with the crosshair. Keep several blocks of open space around it and do not attack it.
steps.success_cue: The Creeper is alive, visible, and can be placed under the center crosshair.

steps.action: Press T to open chat, enter the version-compatible numeric Spectator-mode command exactly as shown, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Spectator mode, can fly through blocks, and can move without interacting normally with blocks or entities.

steps.action: Approach the Creeper in Spectator mode, center the crosshair directly on its body, and press the Attack/Destroy control once—left-click by default—to begin viewing through the Creeper. Do not use right-click.
steps.exact_input: Left-click (Attack/Destroy) once while the crosshair targets the Creeper
steps.success_cue: The camera is locked to the Creeper's position and orientation, independent player movement no longer moves the camera away from it, and the normal Creeper-view green pixelated post-processing shader is active.

steps.action: Without dismounting from the Creeper, changing game mode, toggling perspective, or pressing F4, press T to open chat. Enter the report's command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Because no target argument is supplied, the command acts on the player executing it.
steps.success_cue: The player dies and the death screen containing the Respawn button is displayed.

steps.action: On the death screen, click the Respawn button once. Do not use Return to Title Screen.
steps.success_cue: The death screen closes and the world respawn/loading process begins.

steps.action: Wait until the respawn completes, surrounding chunks and entities have rendered, and movement or camera input responds normally. Make no further perspective, shader, or game-mode changes before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the world after respawning, terrain is visible, and controls respond normally.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has executed /kill while still attached to the Creeper's Spectator-mode viewpoint, clicked Respawn, and completed world loading without making any additional perspective, shader, or game-mode changes. Begin observation of the respawned surroundings now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, world type, difficulty, or dedicated-server requirement. This plan uses a new singleplayer Superflat Creative world at Normal difficulty as a deterministic setup convenience, not as a claimed bug requirement.

The report says to summon a Creeper but does not supply an exact summon command. The plan uses the historical command /summon Creeper ~ ~ ~3, preserving the pre-1.13 entity-name style appropriate to snapshot 14w05a.

The report does not state which method should be used to enter Spectator mode. The numeric command /gamemode 3 was selected because Spectator mode and the numeric value 3 were available in the recommended snapshot.
The report does not state whether controls are rebound. Instructions name both the gameplay action and its default keyboard or mouse input.
